newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SPH SAYS NO PLANS TO CHANGE DUAL LISTING.
newsitem.headline: SPH SAYS NO PLANS TO CHANGE DUAL LISTING.

text.p: Singapore Press Holdings Ltd (SPH) said on Friday it had no plans to change its dual listing of local and foreign share tranches on the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES).
It said in a statement it wished to state it had no plans to change its dual listing status or raise the 49 percent foreign shareholding limit.
This was in response to some discussion in the press lately on dual listing and foreign shareholding limits, it said.
The daily Business Times said on Friday a straw poll among companies with dual listing suggested many would prefer any move to abolish the dual listing to come from monetary authorities.
Earlier Friday, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said it had no intention of asking banks to merge their local and foreign share tranches.
A MAS spokesman said the dual listings depended on the company's limits on foreign shareholdings, and such limits are up to the companies to decide.
